system.description:
In Post-Calamity, the refuse of a hundred factories litter the planet and the cosmos.

Common Salvage · 1 kg · 1 ♄ · d6: 1

Metal scraps that can be used as material for crafting or repairs.

Processors are new thaumaturgicals that require extremely skilled machine labor to even create. Non-corpo machinists and Techgnostics need all the resources they can get.

Common Salvage · 0.25 kg · 50 ♄ · d6: 2

Broken Information Talisman matrices. Cannot function as a processor; can be recycled as repair materials.

Dattreya Wairini was one of the final revolutionaries during the Decades of Carnage, leading the proletariat, the monastery, and the hermitages into a final assault against the Heavendome of Selorong's comprador bourgeoisie. During the final assault her speech ended in three sentences: "Ye proletariat are the hand, the gun, the bullet; I am nothing but the consenter to your Revolution. No one will be free until all are free, until the ultimate emancipation of world and nature! Arise, ye new chakravartins, to fight in the final battle!"

Common Salvage · 0.1 kg · 1 ♄ · d6: 3

A soundstone with a recording of the last three sentences of Dattreya Wairini the Thrice-Awoken's founding speech for the Selorong Commune. Passed down by Commune members; can serve as proof of loyalty to revolutionary ideals.

The abridged version of the Communist Sutra written by Kafeng Masangwa and Fuzi Ekajaya in a 6 fold pamphlet, complete with mantras and holy symbols to turn it into a protective amulet. Easily burned, but easily produced. Sold in Revolution Dharma Temples or subversive Yenjanese Cathedrals.

Common Salvage · 0.2 kg · 1 ♄ · d6: 4

Read at the day's beginning: +1 HRT for the day. Does not stack. After 20 consecutive days of reading, become the target of a Change God's Mind to instill Communism as an Attachment. This begins a Social Project to strengthen the Attachment to a Heart Attachment. By that time, the Cultivator can choose whether to align with Communism or not.

Tsushing was a rice cooker company during the Decades of Carnage that dipped their toes into caravan manufacturing and ship manufacturing during the Second World Revolution. After the Amatsunese Empire was beaten back by the RessenNalenjese, they shifted into electrotechnology: a new industry after revolutions in electrotech. One of their most popular products is the Pressplay PCP, which has revolutionized how music was listened to and therefore how it was made. Pressplays have become ubiquitous especially in the cities, and even revolutionary armies have begun using them for relaying communist studies.

Uncommon Salvage · 0.5 kg · 300 ♄ · d6: 5

A soundstone with reader talismans wrapped into a form familiar to a cassette player. Plays cassette tapes. Includes a headset.

Too Drunk To Ride, an avant-garde, slipstream communist lo-fi shoegaze sonic project, is a failure. The Lovers Rockers was a group of proletarian avant-garde service workers in North Selorong who was too into shoegaze and retropunk and tried to make music off of that. Lovers Rockers ended not long after Too Drunk To Ride, their 4th album, released. Mostly because their recording label, World Mantric Sonarguild, decided that they were getting a bit too… communist with their themes. After disbanding, one of the Lovers Rockers tried to start a board game company.

Common Salvage · 0.1 kg · 50 ♄ · d6: 6

Contains all 21 songs on Lovers Rockers' "Too Drunk To Ride" album. Requires a cassette player.

Handheld flashlights made in the mold of blossoming lotuses with a powerful Light Stone within. Emits strong amounts of light, though must be recharged through chanting.

Common Tool · 0.5 kg · 20 ♄ · d6: 1

Tap and speak a mantra: projects a 10m cone of light, 10m wide at its end. Recharge through chanting.

Kedrat Company is a guild of electrotech mystics and electromachinist monks who sell their wares to any convenience store, grocery, or shop that can afford to buy them and take the vow of peace, vowing to sell it to no state military force. The vow holds power: it is a curse, after all. Should it be sold to a state military, untold misfortune will befall their business and life.

Common Tool · 0.3 kg · 10 ♄ · d6: 2

3-pack. Stores Devil Fuel to power compatible devices made from the 11600s onward.

Common now, especially with the rise of smokes. Various brands have begun producing lighters but the difference is so negligible you could just buy it from any one of them and not really care about the difference.

Common Tool · 0.1 kg · 20 ♄ · d6: 3

40 uses. Flick open to start a small fire. Strikes a Fire Stone.

Handheld radios used as communication receivers. Crafted by Tsunglai Sunggan Engineers during the Second World Revolution, powered by Devil Batteries. Now sold more or less commercially by the Tsunglai Conglomerate—subsumed into HaeCo.

Uncommon Tool · 0.6 kg · 120 ♄ · d6: 4

Communicate with radios tuned to the same frequency. A contraption of soundstone + transmission Talismans, powered by Devil Batteries.

A pocket compass magnetically attuned to the True North. Analog. Haestann Car Industries, under HaeCo, is one of the greatest skyskiff and weapons manufacturer of modern day, and one of the reasons why the United Coalition won in the Second World Revolution. Ultangma Haestann was the one who revolutionized the assembly line, giving birth to "Haestannist Industrialism."

Common Tool · 0.1 kg · 40 ♄ · d6: 5

A magnetic pocket compass. Points to true north: Thule.

Commercial high-focus binoculars by HaeCo. Lets you see really far. Indispensable for assassins, spies, scouts, birdwatchers, firefighters, and so on.

Uncommon Tool · 1 kg · 300 ♄ · d6: 6

See up to 400m. +1 to scouting Checks made using the binoculars. Adjustable focus.

Ylourgne is a popular East Kamguk cosmetics brand supported by the machinations of the Ressen-Nalenjese Confederation. They source their items "ethically" from Dangnu Island.

Uncommon Esotery · 0.5 kg · 200 ♄ · d6: 1

Thaumaturgically enhanced makeup. Eyeliner, lip paint, face powder, mascara (different colors). +1 when interacting with people, +2 if they're attracted to you. -1 to avoiding attention. Lasts for a day or until it's taken off.

Devildrug is made up of six parts brimstone, one part rubydust, one part honey, and one part cinnabar snow. Cinnabar snow can only be created by wizards and alchemists by expelling from their Cultivation Womb and crystallization through Samadhi Fires. It is through Devildrug that firearms were made.

Uncommon Esotery · 0.5 kg · 900 ♄ · d6: 2

While a Cultivator has time and appropriate materials, she can attempt a MND + MACHINE PHYSICS Check to convert this into 10 Bullets.

Otherwise known as an "agimat" in the Isles. Often have yantra diagrams on them. Usually necklaces with transgressive substances within bottles, gold medallions or triangles with potent esoteric-mystic script, or as Alignment-charged esoterica inscribed onto shirts, armors, boots, gloves, and the like. Important people almost always have an agimat on them or two.

Rare Esotery · 0.15 kg · 100,000 ♄ · d6: 3

When the wearer would suffer damage, 1-in-6 chance that the Amulet shatters instead, soaking up to 5 damage.

Awan Rakan was the last of the Solar Kings of Hingsajagra and the Hiyan System. He ruled for 700 years with the sheer power of his Will and the cowing of lesser beings. But time is the medium of dialectics. A legion of lesser gods and mortal heroes overthrew him, and in his end he gasped, seeing the feebleness of his Power.

Rare Esotery · 0.3 kg · 400,000 ♄ · d6: 4

A vial with the dying breath of a God-King, swirling in black and gold. When opened and inhaled, inflicts 3 true damage on the inhaler and then gives them +1 PHYS and WIT for an hour.

Sometime in the 7000s, ancient Razrunan Jagaratthan Mystics fought and killed a Deity named Jarityassera, a Red God who had eaten a thousand spirits from Metom's Furnace. The Mystics ripped open Jarityassera's stomach to reveal that the spirits had been calcified and distilled into ruby hearts within the Red God's stomach. They knew each Heart would grant vitality to whosoever consumed them. And so the Mystics scattered them to the winds. Impossible to commercialize.

Deluxe Esotery · 0.25 kg · 7,777,777 ♄ and impossibly rare · d6: 5

Consume this with a Meal to gain +1 Max HP to a random part.

Catalog note: Add the +1 to the HP bonus of the rolled Part on the sheet.

Jarityassera had a wife, a Blue God named Rawitricheri, a medicinal and magick master. Seri Rawitrisseri gathered her armies of her heaven and sent them crashing into Jagarattha (an ancient Razrunan Kingdom headed by Seri Kangdraputtha) to destroy it in anger. The Mystics rode upon their vimanas and brandished their astras to defeat Rawitrisseri and opened her womb to reveal ten thousand containers for life. They threw this into the wind as well. Impossible to commercialize.

Prestige Esotery · 3 kg · 7,777,777 ♄ and impossibly rare · d6: 6

Consume this with a Meal to gain +1 Max Morale.

Catalog note: Add the +1 to the Morale bonus on the sheet.

Used often by animators and painters that wish to move their paintings. This talisman has smoothed the labor of animators a hundredfold, but it has become a means of the ruling class to eschew hiring skilled animators. The Contradiction intensifies.

Rare Talisman · 0.15 kg · 100,000 ♄ · d6: 1

Nearby 2D objects—paintings, murals, textiles, drawings, shadows, and so on— become sentient for a day and obeys commands to their ability. Cannot leave 2D surfaces but can move through them.

The Intrajala is essentially the internet of Hingsajagra and the nearby Hiyan System Celestial Spheres. It sends data through quantum entanglement vis-a-vis Sidhic Akasha Workings.

Rare Talisman · 0.15 kg · 100,000 ♄ · d6: 2

Project your Consciousness into a nearby Terminal for up to 6 hours. Can travel through the Intrajala purely as a Consciousness, moving through its akashic nexus-space.

A master burglar used this to try and steal a Devil Engine for his community after they've suffered incredible price hikes for electricity. Though the Sidhic Signature was too powerful and led to his torture and arrest by state forces, he managed to teleport all the same.

Rare Talisman · 0.15 kg · 100,000 ♄ · d6: 3

Fold the paper three times and up to three feet can step on it. All that step upon it are teleported to a single location within an urban center that the three of them can clearly visualize. If even one cannot, they have to make a MND + SUSURRATION Check. On a failure, suffer the World's intent: the Intercessor decides what happens.

An incredibly useful talisman in land-locked areas far from rivers, settlements of which have grown ever since the adoption of Capitalism by the World. The knowledge to create these Talismans have been killed. Only talisman-looms can make them now.

Deluxe Talisman · 0.15 kg · 1,000,000 ♄ · d6: 4

Summons potable water enough to fill up a medium sized room from thin air.

A common Talisman during the Esoteric Era, used as a means at destroying others. Rend Talisman creation was controlled by the Wizards. When firearms and Devildrug knowledge arrived, the ability to bypass the high-skill labor of Rend Creation caused Rend to fall out of favor and turned into a niche attack option by scholars and mystics that know of its existence.

Deluxe Talisman · 0.15 kg · 1,999,000 ♄ · d6: 5

Point at a target within sight. Immediately deal [MND] damage to them.

This Talisman was created by the Mystic Arasanjentun who wished to ascend to the heavens with his Dakini Lover. He could not learn the Art of Sky Dancing due to his ill-temper and chose to wield his skill expediently. It is said that when he used this he did fly, but as he reached thin atmospheres he eventually succumbed to the lack of oxygen… and his body never fell to the ground. Some say his Consciousness was captured by his Dakini lover, who placed it in a body fit for someone like him.

Prestige Talisman · 0.15 kg · 1,000,000 ♄ · d6: 6

Gain the ability to fly for one hour. Can go anywhere, but still suffer from thin air pressure and so on.

Catalog note: Printed as a "Prestige Esotery" in the Talismans list. These talismans require destruction to activate (p.191).
